questionBank.subject: Computer Networks
questionBank.text: Which topology requires a multipoint connection where all nodes share a single communication line?
questionBank.explanation: In Bus Topology, all devices are connected along a single backbone cable acting as a multipoint connection.

questionBank.subject: Computer Networks
questionBank.text: What is the primary role of the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP)?
options: Map 32-bit IPv4 address to 48-bit MAC address
Map domain names to IP addresses
questionBank.explanation: ARP resolves logical network layer IP addresses to physical data link layer MAC addresses.

questionBank.subject: Computer Networks
questionBank.text: Which class of IPv4 address provides a default subnet mask of 255.255.0.0?
questionBank.explanation: Class B addresses have a 16-bit network prefix (/16), yielding a default subnet mask of 255.255.0.0.

questionBank.subject: Computer Networks
questionBank.text: What mechanism does TCP utilize to establish a reliable end-to-end full duplex connection?
questionBank.explanation: TCP sets up connection state via a three-way handshake: SYN from client, SYN-ACK from server, ACK from client.

questionBank.subject: Computer Networks
questionBank.text: Which layer of the OSI model handles logical addressing and routing?
questionBank.explanation: The Network Layer (Layer 3) is responsible for packet forwarding, routing, and IP addressing.

questionBank.subject: Computer Networks
questionBank.text: Which of the following protocols is connectionless and does not guarantee packet delivery order?
questionBank.explanation: UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is a lightweight, connectionless protocol without acknowledgments or retransmissions.

questionBank.subject: Computer Networks
questionBank.text: What is the default port number used for secure HTTPS web traffic?
questionBank.explanation: HTTPS operates over TLS/SSL using standardized TCP port 443.

questionBank.subject: Computer Networks
questionBank.text: Which protocol is standardly used by email clients to retrieve messages from a mail server while keeping them synchronized across devices?
questionBank.explanation: IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) stores emails on the server and synchronizes changes across all devices.

questionBank.subject: Computer Networks
questionBank.text: What is the purpose of the Congestion Window (cwnd) in TCP?
options: To prevent the receiver buffer from overflowing
To limit the amount of data injected into the network to avoid congestion
To encrypt payload data against man-in-the-middle attacks
To calculate checksum values for transmission errors
questionBank.explanation: While the receiver advertised window (rwnd) prevents buffer overflow at the receiver, cwnd prevents network congestion.

questionBank.subject: Computer Networks
questionBank.text: Which routing protocol uses Dijkstra algorithm to compute the shortest path tree across link states?
questionBank.explanation: OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) is a link-state routing protocol that utilizes Dijkstra shortest-path-first algorithm.

questionBank.subject: Data Structures
questionBank.text: What is the average time complexity of searching an element in a balanced Binary Search Tree (BST)?
questionBank.explanation: In a balanced BST like AVL or Red-Black tree, the height is logarithmic, giving O(log n) search time.

questionBank.subject: Data Structures
questionBank.text: Which graph traversal algorithm uses a FIFO Queue data structure?
questionBank.explanation: BFS explores neighbor nodes level by level using a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) queue.

questionBank.subject: Data Structures
questionBank.text: What is the worst-case lookup time in a hash table when severe collisions occur and separate chaining is used without treeification?
questionBank.explanation: When all keys hash to the same bucket, the linked chain has length n, resulting in O(n) search time.

questionBank.subject: Data Structures
questionBank.text: In a Min-Heap with N elements, where is the smallest element always located?
questionBank.explanation: In any Min-Heap, every parent is smaller than or equal to its children, meaning the minimum element is at the root.

questionBank.subject: Operating Systems
questionBank.text: Which scheduling algorithm is non-preemptive and selects the process with the smallest execution burst time?
questionBank.explanation: Non-preemptive Shortest Job First schedules the process with the shortest CPU burst next and runs it to completion.

questionBank.subject: Operating Systems
questionBank.text: Which of the following is NOT one of Coffman four necessary conditions for deadlock?
questionBank.explanation: The Coffman condition is "No Preemption". If preemption is allowed, deadlock cannot occur.

questionBank.subject: Operating Systems
questionBank.text: What phenomenon occurs when a page replacement algorithm causes more page faults as the number of allocated physical frames increases?
questionBank.explanation: Belady Anomaly can occur in FIFO page replacement where increasing memory frames increases page faults.

questionBank.subject: Database Systems
questionBank.text: A relation is in Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) if and only if for every functional dependency X -> Y:
options: X is part of a candidate key
questionBank.explanation: BCNF requires that every determinant X in non-trivial functional dependencies X -> Y must be a superkey.

questionBank.subject: Database Systems
questionBank.text: Which ACID property guarantees that concurrent execution of transactions leaves the database in the same state as if transactions were executed serially?
questionBank.explanation: Isolation ensures that concurrent transactions execute independently without interfering with each other.
